sections.heading: The transplant file documents
paragraphs: Before the operation, the transplant centre prepares a file for you and your donor, and in the cases the law specifies the file is presented to the provincial Organ Transplantation Evaluation Commission. The file must include:

If your donor is married, a written declaration is added from the spouse living with the donor stating that the spouse knows of the decision to donate. The commission may request additional documents depending on your case.

Who can donate to you? A relative up to the fourth degree (parents and children, siblings, grandparents and grandchildren, uncles and their children, first cousins), or your husband or wife provided the marriage has lasted at least two years (this condition does not apply if your illness was diagnosed after the marriage). sections.heading: Apostille and translation into Turkish
paragraphs: Algeria has joined the Hague Apostille Convention, which entered into force for it on 9 July 2026; civil status documents no longer need the traditional chain of legalisations when used in member states — a single apostille certificate is enough.

paragraphs: Libya is not a member of the Apostille Convention, so Libyan documents are not stamped with an apostille; instead they go through consular legalisation:

sections.heading: The ethics-commission file (prepared by the transplant centre)
paragraphs: In the cases the law requires — for example if the donor is not a spouse or a relative up to the fourth degree — the file is presented to the Organ Transplantation Evaluation Ethics Commission before the operation. The transplant centre assembles this file and submits it, and it includes, in essence: the identity details of the patient and the donor (the passport for foreign nationals), a report on the donor's capacity to decide, the donor's consent document given before witnesses and approved by a physician, a health report on both parties' suitability for the transplant, a petition explaining the kinship link, and declarations of income and address (and a debts declaration for the donor); and if the donor is married, a declaration from the spouse stating that the spouse knows of the donation. The commission meets every 15 days, and its approval is valid for three months and for one centre only. The patient must also have been registered on the centre's waiting list for at least 3 days before the operation.

sections.heading: Basic conditions for the donor
paragraphs: The donor must be 18 or over, consent freely and without any payment of any kind, and be medically fit as assessed by the transplant team.

faqs.a: Morocco and Türkiye are both parties to the Hague Apostille Convention, in force in Morocco since 14 August 2016 and in Türkiye since 29 September 1985. sections.heading: Entering Türkiye needs no visa
paragraphs: A Moroccan citizen holding an ordinary passport is exempt from a Turkish visa for a stay of up to 90 days. The same exemption applies to the donor and the companion. Make sure your passport is valid for at least six months from your arrival; Turkish law requires the passport's validity to exceed your stay by at least sixty days (that is, 150 days for a ninety-day stay).

bullets: The donor must be an adult (18 or over), donating of his or her own free will with a full understanding of the operation and its risks, and give consent before at least two witnesses, approved by a physician
The donor must be medically fit as assessed by the transplant team, and receive no payment of any kind for the donation

Donation between relatives is allowed up to the fourth degree: parents and children (first); siblings, grandparents and grandchildren (second); uncles and nephews/nieces (third); the closest cousins (fourth)

A husband or wife can donate if the marriage has lasted at least two years (this condition does not apply if the illness that makes the transplant necessary was diagnosed after the marriage), with the duration proven by official documents
If the donor falls outside these degrees, or in the cases the law specifies, the file is subject to ethics-commission approval before the transplant

A copy of the acte de mariage (marriage certificate) if the donor is the husband or wife, or a relative of either

paragraphs: Kinship is not accepted on words; it is proven with official documents. Prepare from the civil status offices in Morocco:

The transplant centre in Türkiye assembles the ethics-commission file and submits it. Under the Turkish regulation the file includes declarations of identity, income and address, a health report on both parties' suitability, a report on the donor's capacity, the donor's attested consent, and a petition explaining where the relationship between you comes from. bullets: The apostille for civil status documents is issued by the local authorities at prefecture or province level (walis and governors, or their deputies), via the official portal apostille.ma

sections.heading: Apostille and sworn translation
paragraphs: Morocco and Türkiye are both parties to the Hague Apostille Convention (in force in Morocco since 14 August 2016, and in Türkiye since 29 September 1985). In practice, your Moroccan civil documents are requested prepared with an apostille certificate and then a sworn translation into Turkish so that the Turkish authorities can rely on them:

bullets: Collect the kinship documents from civil status (family booklet, full copies of birth certificates, marriage certificate where applicable)
Place the apostille on the required documents, then have them translated into Turkish by a sworn translator
Make sure the passports of the patient, the donor and the companion are valid for at least six months

If you are covered by compulsory health insurance (AMO), know that Moroccan law allows you — when treatment cannot be provided inside Morocco — to request prior approval from your insurer (such as the National Social Security Fund, CNSS) to cover the cost of treatment abroad; the final decision rests with the insurer after studying your file, so ask about your case before travelling and do not treat approval as guaranteed
To reach Istanbul, Royal Air Maroc operates direct flights from Casablanca to Istanbul Airport and Sabiha Gökçen Airport, with a flight time of about four hours and forty minutes
sections.heading: Practical steps before travelling
How the review proceeds in Türkiye
paragraphs: After the medical evaluation, the transplant centre submits your file to the provincial ethics commission if your case requires it; the commission meets every 15 days (and immediately in urgent cases), and its approval — when granted — is valid for three months and for that centre only. Complete, consistent documents from the start are the best way to avoid delays. The patient must also have been registered on the centre's waiting list for at least 3 days before the operation.
If you need an official contact inside Morocco, the Embassy of Türkiye is in Rabat (7, Avenue Abdelkrime Benjelloun) and its official website is rabat-emb.mfa.gov.tr.

The Healix team helps you understand the documents the transplant centre asks for and coordinates communication while your file is prepared; the medical evaluation, the submission of the file and the commission's decision belong to the transplant centre and the commission alone.

sections.heading: Entering Türkiye without a visa
paragraphs: Tunisians start the journey with reassuring news: holders of an ordinary Tunisian passport are exempt from a Turkish visa for up to 90 days. This applies to the patient, the donor and the companion, so no advance visa application and no e-Visa is needed.

Just watch your passport's validity: the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs advises that your passport be valid for at least 6 months from your date of arrival, and Turkish law requires the passport's validity to exceed your stay by at least 60 days — that is at least 150 days for a 90-day stay. Check the expiry dates of your passport and your donor's well before booking travel.

bullets: The Livret de famille (family booklet): the reference document showing the family members and their details
An extrait de naissance (birth extract) for both the patient and the donor: issued by the civil status office of the municipality, showing parentage and personal details
An extrait de mariage (marriage extract): if the donor is the husband or wife, or a relative through the spouse
sections.heading: Kinship documents to bring from Tunisia
paragraphs: Living-donor transplantation in Türkiye rests on proving the relationship between you and your donor with official documents — kinship is never accepted on words alone. The Tunisian documents used for this are the official civil status documents:

An important note for married couples: if the donor is your husband or wife, Turkish law requires the marriage to have lasted at least two years (this condition does not apply if the illness that makes the transplant necessary appeared after the marriage), proven by the marriage extract and the family booklet.

If the donor is a relative up to the fourth degree — parents and children (first), siblings, grandparents and grandchildren (second), uncles and nephews/nieces (third), first cousins (fourth) — documented kinship is the basis of the file. If the relationship goes beyond the fourth degree, or there is no kinship, the file goes before the ethics commission before any step is taken.

bullets: Obtain the civil status documents (birth and marriage extracts and the family booklet) from the municipality in Tunisia
Have the apostille placed on them by Tunisian notaries (adouls / عدول الإشهاد) — the sole authority authorised to issue apostilles in Tunisia
Have every document translated into Turkish by a sworn translator
sections.heading: Apostille and sworn Turkish translation
paragraphs: Tunisia and Türkiye are both parties to the Hague Apostille Convention: it entered into force for Tunisia on 30 March 2018, and for Türkiye in 1985. In practice this simplifies preparing your documents:

The transplant centre confirms definitively which documents need the apostille and which only need translation, so prepare the documents in this form from the start to avoid any delay once your file reaches the commission.

bullets: The identity numbers of the patient and the donor (the passport for foreign nationals)
The donor's written consent, given before at least two witnesses and approved by a physician, and a report confirming the donor's capacity to decide
A health report confirming that the patient and the donor are suitable for the transplant, and a physician-approved information form for both
A petition explaining where the relationship between the patient and the donor comes from, supported by the Tunisian kinship documents listed above
Declarations of income level and address from both parties, and a declaration by the donor about any debts
If the donor is married: a written declaration from the spouse living with the donor stating that the spouse knows of the decision to donate
sections.heading: The ethics-commission file in Türkiye
paragraphs: In the cases the law specifies — above all a donor outside the kinship degrees mentioned — your file is presented to the provincial Organ Transplantation Evaluation Ethics Commission. The transplant centre assembles the file and submits it; it includes, in essence:

The commission meets every 15 days, and its approval is valid for 3 months and only for the centre that applied. The patient must also have been registered on the centre's waiting list for at least 3 days before the operation. Complete, consistent documents from the start are the most important factor in avoiding additional questions and delays — and no one can promise you a fixed total period from first evaluation to decision, because that depends on the completeness of your file and your case.

Remember the basic donor conditions: the donor must be an adult (18 or over), donate in complete freedom with a clear understanding of the operation and its risks, be medically fit as assessed by the transplant team, and receive no payment of any kind — donation for payment is a crime under Turkish law, and the commission's checks on this point protect the donor and the patient alike.

sections.heading: Travelling from Tunisia to Istanbul
paragraphs: There are direct flights between Tunis and Istanbul: Tunisair operates flights between Tunis-Carthage Airport (TUN) and Istanbul Airport (IST), and Turkish Airlines also operates direct flights on the same route, taking about three hours. Check the current timetables on both airlines' websites before booking.

ethics-commission-documents-approval.disclaimer: This guide is general information about the ethics-commission review process, published for orientation only. It is not legal or medical advice. The exact documents required in a case, and the outcome of any review, are determined by the transplant centre and the ethics commission under the law in force at the time. HEALIX MEDICAL coordinates communication and takes no part in the decision.

faqs.a: The regulation sets the commission's rhythm: it meets every 15 days, and immediately in emergencies. Once granted, an approval is valid for three months and only for the centre that applied. What no one can promise is a total end-to-end period: the review starts from a complete file, and the overall length depends on the documents provided and the individual case. Preparing complete, consistent documents from the start is the most effective way to avoid delays.
faqs.q: How long does ethics-commission approval take?

faqs.a: It depends on your situation, not only on the relationship. A brother is a second-degree relative, so a donation between siblings normally follows the kinship route without commission review. The commission is always involved where the donor is outside the spouse and fourth-degree relative categories — and also, even between close relatives, where the donor or the patient resides in Türkiye under Law No. 6458. The Ministry may additionally require review for health-tourism patients from regions it designates as risky for organ trade.
faqs.q: Do we need the commission if the donor is my brother?

faqs.a: In practice, documents issued abroad are prepared with a sworn translation into Turkish and an apostille or consular legalisation, so that the transplant centre and the commission can rely on them. The regulation itself does not name these steps; they are requested under the commission's power to require further documents in an individual case. The centre confirms exactly which documents need which form of preparation in your case.
faqs.q: Our documents are in Arabic. What must we do with them?

faqs.a: Yes. Complete documents are necessary but not sufficient: the commission must also be satisfied that the relationship is genuine, that the donor's consent is free and informed, and that no commercial element exists. No hospital or coordinator can change the commission's decision.
faqs.q: Can approval be refused even if all documents are complete?

faqs.a: The transplant centre assembles and submits the file: after its medical evaluation, it registers you and your donor in the Ministry's system and files the application with the provincial ethics commission. HEALIX MEDICAL coordinates communication with the centre and helps you understand what is being asked for, but we do not submit files and we take no part in the decision.
faqs.q: Who submits our file to the commission?

ethics-commission-documents-approval.intro: Before a living-donor transplant can take place in Türkiye in the cases the law specifies, an ethics commission must review and approve the file. This guide explains what the commission is, which documents the regulation requires in every file, which are needed only in specific cases, and how the review proceeds — so that families can prepare properly and avoid unnecessary delays.
ethics-commission-documents-approval.metaDescription: The ethics-commission review for transplants in Türkiye: the documents the regulation makes mandatory in every file, the case-specific documents, foreign documents in practice, and how approval is decided.
ethics-commission-documents-approval.metaTitle: Transplant Ethics Commission in Türkiye – Documents & Approval
ethics-commission-documents-approval.name: The Transplant Ethics Commission: Documents and Approval

sections.heading: What the ethics commission is
paragraphs: The ethics commission — formally, the Organ Transplantation Evaluation Ethics Commission of the province where the application is made — is an official review body that operates under the Organ Transplantation Services Regulation, published in the Official Gazette of 10 December 2022 (No. 32039). Its task is to protect donors and patients: before a transplant takes place, it checks that a proposed living donation is genuine, voluntary and free of any commercial element.

Its review is required whenever a proposed donor is not a spouse or a relative within the fourth degree. It is also required — even between close relatives — where the donor or the patient resides in Türkiye under Law No. 6458, and the Ministry may require it for health-tourism patients from regions it designates as carrying a risk of organ trade, even where the donor is a relative. Without the commission's approval, a transplant in these cases cannot lawfully proceed.

bullets: A declaration of the identity numbers of the patient and the donor (for foreign nationals, in practice their passport or foreign identity number)
A report confirming that the donor has the capacity to decide (is of sound mind — mümeyyiz)
The donor's consent document, given before at least two witnesses and approved by a physician
A physician-approved information form for both the patient and the donor
A health report confirming that both the patient and the donor are suitable for the transplant
A petition explaining where the relationship between the patient and the donor comes from
A declaration of income level from both the patient and the donor
A declaration by the donor stating whether he or she has any debts (donor only)
An address declaration from both the patient and the donor
sections.heading: Documents required in every file
paragraphs: Article 12(6) of the regulation lists the documents that must be present in every ethics-commission application file — the regulation's word is “mandatory” (zorunludur). The transplant centre assembles the file; it contains:

bullets: If the donor is married: a written declaration from the spouse living with the donor, stating that the spouse knows of the decision to donate
Evidence of the relationship — photographs, letters, official kinship documents and similar items — where such evidence exists (the regulation's words are “if available”)
Any further documents the commission itself requires in the individual case, under Article 12(6) of the regulation
sections.heading: Documents required only in specific cases
paragraphs: Three further items appear only where they apply:

sections.heading: Foreign documents: what happens in practice
paragraphs: The regulation does not itself mention apostille, notarisation or sworn translation. In practice, however, civil documents issued abroad — passports, birth and marriage certificates, family records — are requested with an apostille or consular legalisation and a sworn translation into Turkish, so that the centre and the commission can rely on them. This is done under the commission's power to require further documents in the individual case.

Because practice can differ between centres, the transplant centre confirms exactly which of your documents need which form of preparation. Preparing foreign documents in this way from the start avoids delays once the file is with the commission.

bullets: The transplant centre evaluates the patient and the donor medically, and registers both in the Ministry's system
The patient must have been on the centre's waiting list for at least three days before the transplant can take place
The centre — not the patient — files the application with the ethics commission of the province
The commission meets every 15 days (and immediately in emergencies) and examines the relationship, the donor's consent, and whether any payment, coercion or commercial element is present
Only after the commission's approval may the transplant centre schedule the transplant; an approval is valid for three months and applies only to that centre
sections.heading: How the review proceeds
paragraphs: The review follows the medical evaluation: the commission examines a complete file, not an intention. In outline, the process is:

sections.heading: What the commission looks for
paragraphs: Three questions run through every review. Is the stated relationship between patient and donor real and documented? Has the donor decided freely, with a clear understanding of the operation and its risks? And is the donation genuinely unpaid — with no money, gifts or pressure changing hands behind the scenes?

These checks exist because organ trade is a criminal offence under Law No. 2238, and they protect the donor as much as the patient. Complete and consistent documents help the review proceed smoothly; inconsistencies between documents can lead to further questions and delays.

sections.heading: After the decision
paragraphs: If the commission approves the file, the transplant centre can plan the operation with the patient and the donor; the approval remains valid for three months and only for that centre, so the operation is scheduled within that period. If it refuses, the transplant cannot proceed on the basis of that donor file. The regulation fixes the commission's rhythm — a meeting every 15 days — but the total time from first evaluation to decision still varies with the completeness of the file and the individual case, so no end-to-end timetable can be promised.

HEALIX MEDICAL helps families understand which documents the transplant centre is asking for and coordinates communication while the file is prepared. The medical evaluation, the submission of the file and the decision itself belong to the transplant centre and the commission.

ethics-commission-documents-approval.short: What the ethics commission is, the documents the regulation makes mandatory in every living-donor file, the documents required only in specific cases, and how the review proceeds before a transplant in Türkiye can go ahead.

Organ Transplantation Services Regulation (Official Gazette, 10 December 2022, No. 32039)

transplant-law-foreign-patients.disclaimer: This guide is general information about the legal framework, published for orientation only. It is not legal or medical advice. Transplant eligibility, donor acceptance and all approvals are decided by the licensed transplant centre, the ethics commission and the competent authorities under the law in force at the time. HEALIX MEDICAL coordinates communication and does not make these decisions.

faqs.a: Yes. Foreign patients are treated at authorised transplant centres in Türkiye, and living-donor transplantation is the established legal route for them. Before the transplant can proceed, the transplant centre must complete its medical evaluation and, where the law requires it — for donors outside the kinship categories, and for donors or patients residing in Türkiye under Law No. 6458 — the ethics commission must review the file.
faqs.q: Can a foreign patient receive a transplant in Türkiye at all?

faqs.a: First cousins are fourth-degree relatives, which is within the limit for donation based on kinship. The relationship must be proven with official documents. A documented relative within the fourth degree normally follows the kinship route; the commission reviews the file as well only in the specific cases described in this guide — for example, if you or your donor reside in Türkiye under Law No. 6458.
faqs.q: My donor is my cousin. Is that close enough?

faqs.a: Not on the basis of kinship alone. A donor who is not a relative within the fourth degree or a spouse can only be considered with ethics-commission approval, which examines the relationship, the donor's free and informed consent, and that no payment is involved. Approval is a genuine examination and is never guaranteed.
faqs.q: Can an unrelated friend donate to me in Türkiye?

faqs.a: In practice, no. Deceased-donor organs are allocated through the national system to patients on the national waiting list, which serves Turkish citizens and residents. Foreign patients should plan around the living-donor route described in this guide.
faqs.q: Can I join the Turkish waiting list for a deceased-donor organ?

faqs.a: No. HEALIX MEDICAL coordinates communication between you and the transplant centre. Medical eligibility is decided by the transplant team, and where the law requires a legal approval, it is given by the ethics commission. We explain the process and help you prepare the documents the centre asks for.
faqs.q: Does HEALIX MEDICAL decide whether our case is legally acceptable?

transplant-law-foreign-patients.intro: Organ transplantation in Türkiye is governed by a strict legal framework that applies to foreign patients just as it does to Turkish citizens, with additional safeguards for patients who come from abroad. This guide explains, in plain language, the rules that decide who may donate, which approvals are required and which routes are closed. It is general information only: the transplant centre and the competent authorities apply the law to each individual case.
transplant-law-foreign-patients.metaDescription: Turkish transplant law for foreign patients explained: Law No. 2238, living-donor kinship up to the fourth degree, when ethics-commission review is required, and the criminal ban on organ trade.
transplant-law-foreign-patients.metaTitle: Organ Transplant Law in Türkiye for Foreign Patients
transplant-law-foreign-patients.name: Organ Transplant Law in Türkiye for Foreign Patients

sections.heading: The legal framework: Law No. 2238
paragraphs: Transplantation in Türkiye is regulated primarily by Law No. 2238 of 1979, the country's organ and tissue transplantation law, together with the Organ Transplantation Services Regulation, published in the Official Gazette of 10 December 2022 (No. 32039), which sets out how transplant centres and ethics commissions work in practice.

The law applies to every transplant performed in Türkiye, whoever the patient is. Transplants are carried out by authorised hospitals and transplant centres, which apply these rules; patients, relatives and coordination companies cannot set them aside. HEALIX MEDICAL coordinates communication only — it does not evaluate donors and makes no medical or legal decisions.

bullets: First degree: parents and children
Second degree: siblings, grandparents and grandchildren
Third degree: aunts, uncles, nephews and nieces
Fourth degree: first cousins

A spouse — where the marriage has lasted at least two years (this condition is waived if the illness requiring the transplant was diagnosed after the marriage) — and the spouse's relatives within the same degrees
sections.heading: Living donors: kinship up to the fourth degree
paragraphs: A living person may donate a kidney or part of the liver. Where a donation rests on family relationship alone, Turkish law limits it to relatives up to and including the fourth degree, and to a spouse. The degrees are counted from the patient as follows:

sections.heading: When ethics-commission review is required
paragraphs: For some foreign patients, an additional safeguard applies. Where the donor or the patient resides in Türkiye under Law No. 6458 — the law on foreigners and international protection — the file is reviewed by an ethics commission before any transplant can proceed, even if the donor is a close relative. The Ministry may also require the commission's review for health-tourism patients from regions it designates as carrying a risk of organ trade, again even between relatives.

Separately, commission approval is always required whenever a proposed donor is not a spouse or a relative within the degrees above, for Turkish and foreign patients alike. The commission examines whether the relationship is genuine, whether the donor's consent is free and informed, and that no payment or other commercial element is involved. A transplant that requires this approval cannot lawfully proceed without it.

sections.heading: Deceased donation: not a realistic route for foreign patients
paragraphs: Organs from deceased donors in Türkiye are allocated through the national coordination system to patients on the national waiting list, which serves Turkish citizens and residents. In practice, a foreign patient who travels to Türkiye for treatment cannot realistically join that list or receive a deceased-donor organ.

For an international patient, the realistic legal pathway is therefore a living donor who meets the rules on this page, with ethics-commission approval wherever the law requires it. Anyone who suggests otherwise — or who offers a foreign patient a deceased-donor organ for a fee — is describing something the law does not allow.

sections.heading: Organ trade is a crime
paragraphs: Buying or selling an organ, and acting as a broker or intermediary in such a transaction, is a criminal offence under Law No. 2238. Donation must be voluntary and unpaid, and the ethics commission examines files for any sign of a commercial element.

HEALIX MEDICAL does not find, arrange or introduce donors, and no legitimate hospital or coordinator can do so for payment. An offer to “supply” a donor is itself a warning sign of illegal activity, and families should treat it as such.

transplant-law-foreign-patients.short: How Turkish law governs organ transplantation for international patients: living-donor kinship rules, when ethics-commission review is required, and why the deceased-donor waiting list is not a realistic route for foreign patients.
sources: Law No. 6458
Organ Transplantation Services Regulation (Official Gazette, 10 December 2022, No. 32039)

who-can-be-a-living-donor.disclaimer: This guide is general information about the living-donor rules, published for orientation only. It is not legal or medical advice. Whether a specific person may donate is decided by the licensed transplant centre and, where required, the ethics commission, under the law in force at the time. HEALIX MEDICAL coordinates communication and does not assess donors.

faqs.a: Yes, if your marriage has lasted at least two years and the transplant team finds your spouse medically fit to donate. The two-year condition does not apply if the illness requiring the transplant was diagnosed after the marriage. You will need official documents proving the marriage and, where relevant, its duration.
faqs.q: Can my wife or husband donate a kidney to me?

faqs.a: Children are first-degree relatives, the closest category the law recognises. Your child must be at least 18 years old, medically fit, and give free consent before at least two witnesses, approved by a physician. The transplant centre carries out the full medical and legal evaluation.
faqs.q: Can my adult child donate to me?

faqs.a: Only with ethics-commission approval. The commission will examine your relationship, your friend's free and informed consent, and whether any payment or pressure is involved. Approval is a genuine examination, not a formality, and it cannot be promised in advance.
faqs.q: We are not related. Can my friend donate?

faqs.a: No. Donation must be voluntary and unpaid: an organ cannot be bought or sold, and brokering such an arrangement is a criminal offence under Law No. 2238. Any arrangement that looks like payment for the organ itself puts the whole case at risk.
faqs.q: Can a donor be paid for their time or trouble?

faqs.a: The transplant centre checks the documents first; in the cases the law specifies — an unrelated donor, or a donor or patient residing in Türkiye under Law No. 6458 — the ethics commission also reviews the file before the transplant can proceed. That is why official family records, prepared in the form the centre asks for, matter so much.
faqs.q: Who checks that my donor is really my relative?

who-can-be-a-living-donor.intro: Most foreign patients who come to Türkiye for a kidney or liver transplant come with a living donor from their own family. Turkish law sets clear conditions for who may donate and how consent must be given. This guide explains those conditions; the transplant team — and, where required, the ethics commission — decides each individual case.
who-can-be-a-living-donor.metaDescription: Living-donor rules in Türkiye explained: donors must be 18 or over, consent freely before at least two witnesses with a physician's approval, and be relatives to the fourth degree or a spouse — or pass ethics-commission review.
who-can-be-a-living-donor.metaTitle: Who Can Be a Living Donor in Türkiye? – Donor Rules
who-can-be-a-living-donor.name: Who Can Be a Living Donor in Türkiye?

bullets: Be an adult — at least 18 years old
Give consent freely and voluntarily, with a clear understanding of the procedure and its risks
Give that consent before at least two witnesses and have it approved by a physician, as the regulation requires
Be medically fit to donate, as assessed by the transplant team — fitness is never assumed
Receive no payment or other material benefit in exchange for the donation
sections.heading: Conditions every living donor must meet
paragraphs: Whatever the relationship between donor and patient, a living donor in Türkiye must meet all of the following conditions. The transplant centre verifies each one as part of its medical and legal evaluation:

bullets: First degree: parents and children
Second degree: siblings, grandparents and grandchildren
Third degree: aunts, uncles, nephews and nieces
Fourth degree: first cousins
Relatives beyond the fourth degree — such as second cousins — are treated as unrelated donors and need ethics-commission approval
sections.heading: Relatives: donation up to the fourth degree
paragraphs: Where donor and patient are relatives, the law allows donation based on kinship up to and including the fourth degree. The degrees are counted from the patient as follows:

sections.heading: Spouses and the spouse's family
paragraphs: A spouse may donate where the marriage has lasted at least two years. The marriage and its duration are proven with official documents, such as a marriage certificate and family records.

The same kinship framework extends to the spouse's relatives within the degrees described above — for example, a brother-in-law or sister-in-law. As with blood relatives, the relationship must be documented. Whether the file also goes before the ethics commission depends on the case, as the next section explains.

sections.heading: Unrelated donors: only with ethics-commission approval
paragraphs: A family friend, a colleague or any other person outside the degrees above is an unrelated donor. Such a donation cannot rest on kinship, so it can only be considered after approval by the ethics commission, which examines the genuineness of the relationship, the donor's free and informed consent, and the absence of any payment or coercion.

Two further groups always go before the commission, even between close relatives: cases where the donor or the patient resides in Türkiye under Law No. 6458, and — where the Ministry so decides — health-tourism patients from regions it designates as risky for organ trade. Families in these situations should treat the commission stage as a standard, expected part of the process — not as an obstacle, and not as a formality that can be skipped.

bullets: Family registry extracts or birth certificates showing the family relationship
A marriage certificate where the donor is a spouse or a spouse's relative
In practice, a sworn translation into Turkish of each document issued abroad
In practice, apostille or consular legalisation of foreign civil documents, where the centre or the commission requires it
sections.heading: Proving the relationship
paragraphs: Kinship is never taken on trust. The transplant centre asks for official documents that show the relationship between patient and donor, and documents issued abroad must be prepared so that the Turkish authorities can rely on them:

who-can-be-a-living-donor.short: The conditions every living kidney or liver donor in Türkiye must meet: adult age, free consent given before witnesses and approved by a physician, kinship up to the fourth degree, spouses — and ethics-commission approval for everyone else.
sources: Law No. 6458
Organ Transplantation Services Regulation (Official Gazette, 10 December 2022, No. 32039)
